hero.body: Two decades at one bench in Sweifieh. No moulds, no repeats — each setting is cut to the stone it will hold.

marquee: Turquoise · Carnelian · Amethyst · River pearl · 18K gold · Hand-engraved · Amman ·

collection.title:
Three pieces,
none repeated
collection.body: What is on the bench this season. When a piece leaves the workshop, its design leaves with it.

ring.name: Nishapur Signet
ring.blurb: A rectangular Nishapur cabochon held in twisted gold rope, with two Yemeni carnelians set into the shoulders.
ring.detail: The turquoise was cut in Mashhad and left unbacked, so the matrix reads as it did in the vein. The rope bezel is drawn by hand from a single wire, then closed at the base where the join will never be seen. Shoulders are hammered, not cast — the texture holds light at the edges instead of flattening it.

necklace.name: Carnelian Roundel
necklace.blurb: A deep carnelian disc with a hand-engraved gold rosette at its centre, hung from a turquoise-capped bail.
necklace.detail: The rosette is chased directly into the gold with a set of gravers ground for this workshop. The carnelian is Yemeni, chosen for the darker end of the range where the red carries almost no orange. The toggle bar is functional — it locks, it does not decorate.

set.name: Amethyst & Pearl Suite
set.blurb: Paired cabochons — one pearl, one amethyst — in pierced gold crowns, on a box chain drawn in the workshop.
set.detail: Each crown is pierced by hand so light passes behind the stone rather than stopping at the metal. The pearls are matched for overtone, not only for size, which is why a suite can take a season to complete. The box chain is drawn and soldered link by link.

craft.title:
Four hours
of filing for
one surface
craft.body: Nothing here is finished by machine. The sequence below is the same one Bashar was taught at fourteen, and it has not been shortened since.

one.title: The stone comes first
one.body: A piece begins when a stone is worth building around. Nothing is designed and then filled.

two.title: Wire drawn by hand
two.body: Gold is drawn down through the plate to the gauge the setting needs — never bought pre-formed.

three.title: Set cold, closed once
three.body: The bezel is burnished over the stone without heat. There is one attempt; a second would mark the gold.

four.title: Signed underneath
four.body: The workshop mark and karat are stamped where only the wearer will find them.

stones.title:
Four stones,
sourced the same way
for fifty years

turquoise.name: Turquoise
turquoise.note: Sky-blue with a fine brown matrix. Left unbacked and unstabilised.

carnelian.name: Carnelian
carnelian.note: Cut from the darker seam, where the red holds without turning orange.

amethyst.name: Amethyst
amethyst.note: Cabochon, never faceted — the depth of colour does the work.

pearl.name: River pearl
pearl.note: Matched by overtone before size. A matched pair can take months.

atelier.quote: Copies can look alike. What they cannot carry is the story of the original, its craft, or its authenticity.
atelier.body1: The workshop has been in Sweifieh for close to twenty years, on Subhi Al-Omari Street. Two benches, four hands, and a drawer of gravers older than anyone using them. In that time our designs have been copied often enough that we take it as the measure.
atelier.body2: We do not hold stock. A piece is made when someone asks for it, and the stone is chosen with them — in the room, under daylight, before a single line is drawn.

visit.title:
Come and
hold it first
visit.body: Fittings are by appointment so the bench can be cleared and the stones laid out for you. Tell us roughly what you have in mind — we will bring options.
